title: Tinyfloat Uniformity Probe — Personal Lab Dump
content:
Quick brain dump from my bench sessions. Goal: see whether tinyfloat value distribution (fp8/tiny formats) creates non-uniform buckets that correlate with NaN spikes in attention/kvcache. This is a scratchpad — rough, partial, many TODOs.

Background/context:
- Incident: intermittent NaN in production when scaling seq-len to 4096 in prod-dedicated pools (saw spikes in Feb 2026 window).
- Hypothesis: quantization of intermediate attention scores/softmax logits into tinyfloat (FP8-ish) creates underflow/overflow/uniformity problems for certain ranges, amplified by RNG/weight initialization seeds and layernorm edge-values.
- Why tinyfloat? We rolled integer/8-bit and fp8 variants as cost experiment. Tinyfloat kernels are newer (experimental) and not as exercised.

What I tried (commands & notes):
1) Minimal repro runner (local colab-style):
- python repro_tinyfloat_probe.py --model small-8b --quant fp8 --seq-len 4096 --batch 1 --seed 42 --cache-policy none
- Observed: intermittent NaN at step ~115 (non-deterministic across runs).

2) Iterative narrowing (quick loop):
- for s in 0 1 2 3 42 1234 9999; do python repro_tinyfloat_probe.py --seed $s --runs 50 --quant fp8; done
- Findings: seeds {42,1234,9999} produced NaN 30–60% of runs; seeds {0,1,2,3} much lower. Pattern suggests sampling of activations intersects a bad quantization boundary.

3) Kernel-level toggles (local docker whl):
- export RW_DISABLE_KV_CACHE=1
- export RW_TINYFLOAT_STOCHASTIC=1
- python -m rwinfer.serving --model small-8b --quant fp8 --trace nan_trace.log
- With STOCHASTIC turned on, NaN frequency drops but does not vanish. With CACHE disabled, NaN frequency also drops. Hmm — caching + tinyfloat interaction.

4) Instrumentation snippets I added to runtime (pseudocode):
- if isnan(out).any():
-    dump({"layer": i, "pre_q_stats": pre_quant_stats.tolist(), "post_q_stats": post_quant_stats.tolist(), "seed": rng.get_state()})
- That produced arrays where post_quant had many identical low-mantissa bins (flat tails).

Raw error snippets from traces:
- RuntimeError: Kernel produced NaN in matmul output at layer 9 (kv cache write)
- Warning: quantizer overflow detected: value clipped to max_bin
- Trace excerpt: [0.00023, 0.00023, 0.00023, 0.00023, 0.00023, 3.2e+03, NaN] — sudden jump then NaN

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Tinyfloat encoding uses a too-small exponent bias for certain attention score ranges => overflow-to-NaN after softmax normalization when combined with denorms. (High confidence)
- H2: Deterministic prefix caching + stale KV quantization leads to repeated identical bins; downstream stable values amplify rounding to exact same tinyfloat codepoint and that triggers a codepath that mishandles denorms (e.g., a divide by zero after normalization). (Medium)
- H3: RNG/state divergence (different ordering of operations between CPU sched/TPU) causes unlucky combination of values that hits under-tested vectorized path in CUDA kernels. (Low-medium)

Quick tests to distinguish H1 vs H2:
- Force full-precision (BF16) for softmax input only: python repro_tinyfloat_probe.py --quant fp8 --force-softmax-bf16
  - Result: NaN vanished in >200 runs. Strong signal that softmax quant path important.
- Re-run with cache disabled: NaN reduced significantly. That bakes into H2.

Exploratory metrics I collected (samples):
- pre_quant distribution (layer9 logits): mean=0.12, std=0.93, min=-23.1, max=3200
- post_quant unique_bins (layer9): 6 out of 256 used in tail region; majority collapsed to one bin for many tokens
- denorm count after quant: nonzero but small (approx 0.8% of tokens) when seed=42; but when seed=1234 denorm count => 4.9%

Small repro variants I tried:
- clip_logits(clip_val=50) before quant => NaN eliminated in local runs. (This suggests overflow-to-NaN from extreme logits.)
- add tiny epsilon before softmax denom (eps=1e-6) => reduced NaN frequency but not gone.
- increase exponent bits in simulated tinyfloat (simulator) from 5->6 => eliminates NaN.

Actionable next steps (short):
- Add defensive clipping in softmax quant path (clip to +/- 1000) and add optional config flag RW_FP8_CLIP_LOGITS. Quick patch + e2e test.
- Add test harness that fuzzes seed/seq-len/batch to produce distribution heatmaps for pre/post quant. Put under experiments/quant-fuzz (link to RED-3179).
- Rework denorm handling path in CUDA kernel: ensure we canonicalize denorms to flushed-zero or normalized representation before any divide. Needs kernel owner review. (Pinged @Riley)
- Add telemetry: histogram of unique_bins per-layer, per-request; alarm if unique_bins < 10 for >1% of tokens.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Is there an upstream standard for fp8 tinyfloat exponent bias across frameworks? Check NVIDIA docs and FP8 draft (TODO).
- If we clip logits server-side, we might change model behavior — need to coordinate with models team and run quality evals on a small prompt set.
- Investigate whether mixed-precision BF16 fallback for softmax can be enabled as a per-route policy in Console as quick mitigation (per-customer toggle).

Quick reproduction file skeleton (repro_tinyfloat_probe.py) — summary of key parts:
- load model in eval mode, set quant config
- seed RNGs (torch, numpy, random)
- run prompt loop until NaN or max_steps, log pre/post quant histograms
- toggles: --force-softmax-bf16, --disable-kv-cache, --stochastic-quant

Last run notes (2026-02-20):
- With temporary clip and force-softmax-bf16 enabled, no NaN across 500 runs for seq-len 4096. Need to validate on dedicated clusters and with heavier concurrency.

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Draft PR with softmax clipping (small opt-in flag)
- [ ] Add fuzz harness + automated flakes run in CI (nightly)
- [ ] Get kernel owner sign-off for denorm handling change
- [ ] Schedule review with models team for quality regression tests

Random ideas (brainstorm):
- Could we implement adaptive exponent scaling per-layer (scale logits down progressively when max>threshold) as a smoother alternative to hard clipping? Could be parameterized and learned via small calibration run.
- A/B route-level toggles: fallback to bf16-softmax for enterprise customers during incidents.

End of dump. Will flesh out and convert to PR notes once I triage kernels with Riley.
